title: Check
description: A single automated check that verifies a spec's acceptance criteria.

spec.description: Rule ID this check belongs to. Used only by per-repo checks in spex.yaml, where the check's identity is `<spec>/<name>`; omitted inside rule files, which supply the rule ID themselves.

description.description: Optional human-readable summary of what the check verifies.

type.description: How the check is executed: regexp matches file contents, glob matches file paths, ast-grep matches a code structure, script runs an external program.

severity.description: Severity when the check fails. Defaults to error when omitted.

include.description: Glob patterns that narrow this check's file set to matching paths. When omitted, all non-ignored files are in scope.

exclude.description: Glob patterns that remove matching paths from this check's file set.

pattern.description: Regular expression matched against the contents of each in-scope file.

negate.description: Inverts the check. When false (default), a match is a violation (forbidden). When true, a file with no match is a violation (required).

pattern.description: Path glob matched against the paths of in-scope files.

negate.description: Inverts the check. When false (default), a matching path is a violation (forbidden). When true, the absence of any matching path is a violation (required).

then.description: Structural, AST-based match using ast-grep (https://ast-grep.github.io/), backed by tree-sitter. More precise than `regexp` for code patterns: matches by syntax tree shape, so it ignores comments/strings and tolerates reformatting, and can express relational constraints (a node inside/not-inside another, argument text matching a sub-pattern) that plain text matching cannot.

language.description: ast-grep language id (e.g. `typescript`, `tsx`, `javascript`, `python`, `go`, `rust`, `java`). Omitted: inferred per file from its extension, and files with no matching language are skipped.

pattern.description: An ast-grep structural pattern, e.g. `console.log($$$ARGS)`. `$VAR` binds one node, `$$$VAR` binds a list of nodes. Mutually exclusive with `rule`.

rule.description: A full ast-grep rule object: `{rule: <atomic|relational|composite rule>, constraints: {<metavariable>: <rule>}}`. Supports `pattern`, `kind`, `regex`, `inside`, `has`, `not`, `all`, `any`, and metavariable `constraints` — see https://ast-grep.github.io/reference/yaml.html. Mutually exclusive with `pattern`.

negate.description: Inverts the check. When false (default), a match is a violation (forbidden). When true, a file with no match is a violation (required).

then.description: Runs an external script stored in the spex directory at `scripts/<rule-id>/<script>`.

script.description: Script filename (for example `writing-style.sh`). Resolved in the spex directory at `scripts/<rule-id>/<script>`, so the `<rule-id>` folder keeps checks from different rules from sharing a path.

run.description: Invocation granularity. `per-file` runs the script with the matched files (after include/exclude) as arguments. `per-repo` runs it once per governed repository with no arguments. `workspace` runs it exactly once with no arguments
